To build peace one young person at a time.

Rotary has organised international youth exchanges for 55 years. Youth exchange is in Rotary\'s DNA: young people hold the future, for Rotary and for the world. Since 2010, youth service with youth exchange has been Rotary\'s fifth Avenue of Service. Every year there are 7,000 exchanges worldwide. In the Netherlands, the Multi-District Youth Committee (MDJC) organises them.

The rules and the code of conduct of the exchange programme.

How wonderful that your Rotary club wants to sponsor an exchange student, and so also receive and support a student from abroad in your club for a year. Perhaps a student approached you, or the wish came from one of your members.

A Rotary club sponsors a student who wants to spend a school year abroad as an ambassador of Rotary International. This is open to all young people, from Rotary families and beyond. In the same year the club receives a student from abroad, who goes to school here with peers and lives with two to at most four host families during the year.
As a guideline, students sent and received are 15½ to 18½ years old.

The exchange is reciprocal: every Rotary club that sends a student abroad receives an exchange student in the same year. The student lives with several host families during the year, whom the club visits beforehand.
Sponsoring a Dutch student costs your club nothing. Hosting an exchange student does, and the one cannot happen without the other.

For a whole school year, hosting costs your club at most € 2,000. The national organisation MDJC finds the programme so important that it gives every hosting club a subsidy of € 1,250. Your club then pays at most € 750 for the whole year.

Together with the student who wants to go abroad, the club youth commissioner finds three host families and a reserve family. Children of the same age in the family are nice but not needed: with them a student finds friends sooner, but older couples are often wonderful host parents, and in families with young children a student often learns Dutch faster.
Working with another Rotary club can be a good choice and gives more ways to find host families.

Former exchange students are happy to come and tell your club about their experiences, to inform it or get it enthusiastic. For more information, ask the members of the MDJC or your district youth commissioner.
